title: Unified Inference: Product overview, PRD, roadmap, pricing & release notes (Aug 2026)
author: Jordan Kim
content:
SUMMARY
-------
This document consolidates the product overview, high-level PRD (requirements & acceptance criteria), key design specifications, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product line (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private). It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and customer success stakeholders preparing for the Q3–Q4 2026 rollout wave.

BACKGROUND
----------
Redwood's Unified Inference initiative unifies our developer surface and operational controls across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments. Customers increasingly request:
- Predictable latency and throughput across deployment modes
- Transparent unit economics and pricing guidance for mixed workloads
- Operational primitives for safe rollouts and model fallbacks

GOALS (Q3–Q4 2026)
-------------------
1. Provide a single API and config model for generation, chat, and embeddings with consistent semantics.
2. Ship pricing tiers and packaging for Hosted, Dedicated commit, and Private licenses that align with expected unit economics.
3. Deliver observability & rollout features: per-route dashboards, canary rollouts, automatic fallback policies.
4. Achieve production SLOs for majority of customer workloads (see SLO table below).

PRD: REQUIREMENTS & ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
--------------------------------------
1) Core API compatibility
   - Requirement: One REST/SDK surface with endpoints for /generate, /chat, /embeddings and unified request schema.
   - Acceptance: SDK tests pass across Python/Node/Go; examples in quickstarts produce identical outputs (within nondeterminism bounds) for supplied prompts.

2) Model Rollouts & Fallbacks
   - Requirement: Per-route rollout policy with canary % and automatic fallback to pinned compatible model variant when SLOs breach.
   - Acceptance: Runbook validation where simulated capacity depletion triggers fallback within 30s and error rate for end-users remains < 1%.

3) Observability & Cost Attribution
   - Requirement: Token-level cost breakdown, p95/p99 latency per model, and per-route utilization charts.
   - Acceptance: Dashboards show accurate cost attribution for at least 3 synthetic workloads; billing events match observed token usage within 0.5%.

4) Dedicated & Private Packaging
   - Requirement: Offer three Dedicated commit tiers (S, M, L) with autoscaling and burst; Private license packaged with optional on-prem install and KMS integration.
   - Acceptance: Capability validated in staging with a pilot customer on Dedicated M and one Private on-prem deployment using Customer KMS.

5) Performance & Reliability SLOs
   - Requirement: Target SLOs must be documented and tested.
   - Acceptance: Benchmark suite demonstrates SLOs for representative models.

SLOs (Target)
-------------
| Deployment | Latency p95 (tokens/sec equiv) | Availability (monthly) | Error budget |
| Hosted (small models) | p95 <= 200ms for streaming first token | 99.9% | 43.2 minutes |
| Hosted (large models) | p95 <= 800ms first token | 99.5% | 3.65 hours |
| Dedicated | p95 <= 250ms (pinned capacity) | 99.95% | 21.6 minutes |
| Private (on-prem) | operationally-targeted; guidance only | customer-managed | n/a |

DESIGN SPECIFICATIONS (HIGH-LEVEL)
----------------------------------
1) API surface\   - Endpoints: POST /v1/generate, POST /v1/chat, POST /v1/embeddings\   - Unified request fields: model, input, temperature, max_tokens, stop, route_policy, rollout_policy_id\   - Streaming: server-sent events (SSE) and websocket SDK fallbacks supported\\n2) Rollout policy model\   - Policies: immediate, gradual-canary (steps by percentage, duration), time-windowed, traffic-split\   - Fallback triggers: latency breach (p95 threshold), error rate breach (> 1% over 5m), capacity saturation (queue depth > threshold)\   - Owner: eng-platform rollout team (primary) with product owning policy UX\\n3) Observability & Telemetry\   - Telemetry events: request.start, request.token.generated, request.end, model.fallback, billing.charge\   - Dashboards: per-route latency, cost-per-token heatmap, token-usage histogram, recent rollout events\\n4) Serving runtime integration points\   - Model variants: quantized (q4_0), fp16, and low-latency sharded variants supported\   - Kernel selection: heuristics based on model size, sequence length distribution, and hardware label\   - Caching: prefix KV caching configurable per route (ttl, cache-hit routing)\\n5) Security & Compliance\   - Private deployments must support HSM/KMS, audit logging (immutable S3 bucket), and network isolation (VPC peering).

ARCHITECTURE DIAGRAM (text)
---------------------------
API Gateway -> Router (policy engine) -> Model Serving Fleet (hosted/dedicated/private)\                          -> Observability pipeline (metrics/traces)\                          -> Billing pipeline (token events -> aggregation)

ROADMAP & THEMES (next 6 months)
-------------------------------
- Q3 2026 (Aug–Sep): Finalize PRD, open beta for rollout policies, publish pricing guidance. Owners: Product (Jordan Kim), Eng-Platform (Priya Nair).
- Q4 2026 (Oct–Dec): GA for Unified API; Dedicated tier launches; Private v1 packaging and early enterprise pilots. Owners: Sales/GTM + Eng-Private-Deployments.
- 2027 H1: Optimize unification for multi-region routing, advanced cost optimization (auto-batching suggestions), and expanded model catalog.

Roadmap milestones (dates are target)
1. 2026-08-15: PRD approved (this doc).
2. 2026-09-20: Beta release of rollout & fallback policies; documentation and quickstarts published.
3. 2026-11-01: Dedicated S/M tiers GA (reserved capacity + burst).
4. 2026-12-10: Unified API GA for Hosted; Private v1 license available for pilot customers.

PRICING & PACKAGING NOTES (Guidance)
------------------------------------
Note: Pricing below is guidance for sales and packaging teams. Finalized pricing to be pushed to pricing-portal after finance review.

1) Hosted API (public, usage-based)\   - Generation: $0.018 per 1k input tokens, $0.06 per 1k output tokens for large models (example tier).\   - Embeddings: $0.0007 per embedding (128-d standard).\   - Discounts: volume tiers at 5% / 12% / 20% at monthly usage thresholds $100k / $300k / $1M.\\n2) Dedicated (reserved capacity)\   - Tier S: $15k/month (4 GPU-equivalent), baseline throughput X tokens/sec, 5% discount on overages.\   - Tier M: $50k/month (16 GPU-equivalent), predictable latency SLO, 10% discount on overages.\   - Tier L: $150k/month (48 GPU-equivalent), SLA-backed 99.95% availability, priority capacity.\   - Burst: optional burst pool charged at $0.08 per 1k tokens consumed when capacity exceeded.\\n3) Private (enterprise license)\   - Base license: platform fee (one-time) + annual support (10–20% of license) + optional professional services for on-prem installation.\   - KMS/HSM integration, audit logging, and extended retention packaged as add-ons.\\nPackaging notes for sales\n- Offer a Migration Pack: 2-week onboarding, integration runbook, and a pilot quota conversion to credits.\- Guarantee: For Dedicated contracts > $300k ARR, offer a migration discount and extended onboarding.

CUSTOMER MIGRATION & ROLLOUT PLAYBOOK (high-level)
--------------------------------------------------
1) Discovery & sizing: run capacity estimator with customer's request traces (owner: solutions engineering).
2) Pilot: deploy Dedicated M or Hosted with traffic shadowing for 2 weeks.
3) Canary: configure gradual-canary with 5%, 25%, 50%, 100% steps over configurable durations.
4) Cutover: full traffic cutover with rollback window and validated SLOs.

RELEASE NOTES (2026-08.15 snapshot)
----------------------------------
Release: Unified Inference PRD + Beta rollout feature set\- New: Unified API spec (generate/chat/embeddings) and SDK updates (Python/Node/Go).\- New: Rollout policies (gradual canary, automatic fallback) shipped to beta customers.\- New: Pricing guidance published for Hosted & Dedicated tiers (internal only).\- Improved: Observability telemetry keys for token-level cost attribution.\- Fixed: Several known issues related to streaming timeouts on multi-chunk responses.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS & RISKS
------------------------
- Private on-prem installations depend on customer network and storage; SLOs are operationally defined and cannot be guaranteed by Redwood.
- Pricing guidance is provisional and subject to finance/legal approval.
- Rollout policy UX needs additional iteration based on early beta feedback (expected changes to policy step UI).

METRICS & KPIs TO TRACK
-----------------------
- Adoption: number of customers using Unified API (target 150 by EOY 2026).
- Revenue mix: % revenue from Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Performance: % of routes meeting p95 latency SLO (target 95% of routes).
- Cost: average tokens/sec per GPU and cost per 1k tokens across top 10 workloads.

APPENDICES
---------
A. Example API request (curl)
----------------------------
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-unified-1","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":256,"rollout_policy_id":"canary-2026-09"}'

B. Acceptance test checklist (engineering)
----------------------------------------
1) SDK integration tests green across Python/Node/Go.
2) Rollout simulation: capacity depletion scenario exercises fallback logic.
3) Billing reconciliation: token events aggregated and checked against billing pipeline.
4) Performance: benchmark harness demonstrates p95 latency targets for representative models.
